articles.title: Portland’s working waterfront is no place for professional soccer
articles.author: Pine and Roses -- Maine DSA
articles.content_excerpt: I love the Hearts of Pine. Been to my share of games. Have spent hundreds of bucks on gear. I’m on a first name basis with one of the owners. And I appreciated the statement they made last month calling for accountability after ICE murdered Johan Sebastian Guerrero Duran. All that said, the city of Portland should not carve out an exception to our working waterfront zone in order to allow them to build a $50 million dollar soccer stadium on land protected for marine-based industries. Why? Well, soccer stadiums can operate anywhere. Cargo ships, barges, trawlers, and tugboats cannot. Nor can the longshoremen and women, stevedores, harbor pilots, and deckhands who service them. articles.title: Gloria Steinem Was No Enemy of the Left
articles.author: Daniel Geary
articles.content_excerpt: In 2016, Gloria Steinem backed Hillary Clinton and dismissed young women who supported Bernie Sanders as doing so only because “the boys are with Bernie.” (She later said she misspoke). After her death last week, Steinem has been extravagantly praised in the mainstream media. Is it any wonder, then, that some leftists see Gloria Steinem as the “godmother of neoliberal feminism”?Yet left-wing dismissals and establishment celebrations both have Steinem wrong.At the height of her influence in the 1960s and ’70s, when she was a leading spokesperson for women’s liberation, Steinem was very much on the Left. articles.author: Garrison Lovely
articles.content_excerpt: Not long ago, a close friend of mine, a software engineer, was discussing how his job role had changed in recent months as his company had moved to adopt an “AI-first approach.” He explained that this approach had altered his team’s dynamics. articles.title: How the Left Can Win a Supermajority
articles.author: Jared Abbott
articles.content_excerpt: Adam Jentleson’s Supermajority: How Democrats Can Build Lasting Power challenges us to think longer term about what it would take to halt the steady march of right-wing authoritarianism and deliver durable but long-overdue relief for working Americans. Its premise is simple: the only way to get from here to a basically social democratic future (not his words) is to consistently win supermajorities in Congress, and the only way to do that is for Democrats to become competitive again in more red states. Flipping a six-to-three Supreme Court means holding the Senate across multiple cycles, which means maintaining something near sixty seats. articles.title: Britain’s Health Crisis Is Becoming a Political Crisis
articles.author: Jatinder Hayre
articles.content_excerpt: Britain is becoming a sicker country. A country in which millions of people can expect to spend an increasing share of their lives in poor health is not just a recipe for a social crisis but a political one too. The latest figures are extraordinary. Healthy life expectancy in the United Kingdom has fallen to its lowest level since the present Office for National Statistics series began in 2011 to 2013. A boy born today can expect around 60.7 years of good health; for a girl, the figure is 60.9. Yet even these averages conceal the more disturbing story. In the most deprived areas of England, healthy life expectancy is just 49.8 years for men and 48.2 for women. In the least deprived areas, it reaches 69.2 and 68.5 years, respectively. Measured across the deprivation gradient, the gap is 19.

articles.title: Germany’s Far Right Is Close to Power. Appeals to “Defend Democracy” Won’t Stop It.
articles.author: Thomas Zimmermann
articles.content_excerpt: In Sunday’s state election in Saxony-Anhalt, local Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) lead candidate Ulrich Siegmund ran on the slogan “Anything Is Possible.” Those same words could serve as the headline for political forecasts the day after the vote. For while the election produced a clear winner, it didn’t yield a definitive outcome. While the far-right AfD scored an impressive 43.8 percent of votes cast, it has not secured an absolute majority. Nor does the anti-AfD camp have a majority, as Sahra Wagenknecht’s party — Bündnis Sahra Wagenknecht (BW), a split from the socialist Die Linke — stands in between the two sides. articles.title: Rust Belt Rising
articles.author: Rochester Red Star: News from Rochester DSA
articles.content_excerpt: by Hannah W. The first ever Rust Belt Rising conference was held on August 15th and 16th here in Rochester. This was organized by Workers Assembly of Rochester (WAR), an independent organization of local labor activists, including DSA members, union staffers and organizers. Local labor leaders, rank and file members and members of community organizations gathered to discuss and learn about the role of the labor movement in Rochester, and how we can move it to be more militant and left.
